The Senator pledged that he and his fellow Democrats in the Senate will continue to fight for every child’s access to a good education.

children: Treasury Targets Race-Based Bias in Schools

Schumer’s criticism came as the Treasury and IRS, on Thursday, proposed rules to strip tax-exempt status from private schools that discriminate based on race, color or national origin. The proposal, which Treasury and the IRS say implements President Trump’s executive orders, would cover admissions, scholarships, athletics and other programs at as many as 18,000 institutions.

Schools could still use race-neutral criteria, such as family income, geographic location, first-generation status, individual hardship, military family status, or academic achievement to support disadvantaged students, with rules taking effect in 2027.
"Schools rebranding race-based preferences as equitable, inclusive, or diversity-enhancing does not change their discriminatory nature,” said the Treasury.
